findings: Kernel check (python, exact integers): the 51-element free-RIGHTSN(3) model satisfies zyx=zxzyx and fails xyz=xyzxz, xyzx=xyxzx and zyx=zxyx. So RIGHTSN (locally right regular) coincides on 3 generators with the standard right seminormal variety RSNB; general equality is a named literature identification, not proved here.

Group-actor scope: the group case of item4 (E-unitary orthodox S with RSNB idempotent band) is exactly the right-seminormal part of the statement Billhardt (J. Algebra 206 (1998) 40-50, Section 3) attributes to M. B. Szendrei (private communication): every E-unitary regular semigroup with seminormal band is strictly embeddable. Not reconstructed; no published proof located.

Written reductions (same-author, unreviewed): CS actors with one row, one column, or a rectangular-group actor reduce to the group case (then E(S) is a band; rows R_i are E-unitary over G via theta_i(s)=g_s p_{lambda_s,i}).

Written observation: 'one-layer retraction bands' Const(Omega) ∪ {retractions onto a fixed G-invariant F ⊆ Omega} are RSNB (local monoids are {r} ∪ Const(F) ≅ RZ^1), and B5 is exactly the case |Omega|=3, |F|=2. Two nested retraction layers are generally NOT RSNB.

Kernel analysis of a 14-element RRL source (top group C2 over a CS ideal K with column 0 doubled) shows its local R-pair is separated exactly by such a one-layer band: constants = C2-labelled K-columns modulo the top group's right action, retractions = top elements.
